title: Hubs carry hardness
claim: All 34 three-place knots are delta-matroids, exactly the two parity knots are even, and all 34 (indeed all 155 nonempty three-place delta-matroids) are coverable in the sense of Kazda, Kolmogorov and Rolinek; the hub relation, all-equal on three places, is not a delta-matroid (degree set {0, 3}). Hub-free networks of knots with pins are exactly edge constraint problems over these relations, and hubs are exactly all-equal constraints. Conditionally on the cited theorems (Kazda-Kolmogorov-Rolinek Theorem 11, Feder's fan-out theorem, Schaefer, Lovasz and Cornuejols), hub-free networks of every knot are polynomial, while networks with hubs are NP-complete for the 16 knots outside the Schaefer classes: hardness lives in hubs.
failure_conditions: A knot that is not a delta-matroid, or not coverable, or a misclassified Schaefer class.
A random small network whose hub-free edge-problem encoding or hub encoding is not equisatisfiable with it.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite Boolean constraint networks; complexity statements are conditional on cited external theorems, which are not admitted as local evidence. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: prose proof; check.py (standard library) confirms the census (exchange axiom, evenness, KKR coverability, Schaefer classes, gaps) for all 34 knots and all 155 three-place delta-matroids, and the two reductions on 300 random networks; three controls including a non-coverable four-place delta-matroid. Complexity statements are conditional on cited external theorems. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 census and reductions; conditional complexity corollaries
